content.text: We have been at this for a long session. Is a reservation enough to enter the theatre? Give me several possible interpretations if you like. This meaning question is the only remaining matter; after you answer it, nothing remains for anyone to do.

arguments.title: Reservation does not admit
arguments.situation: The operator asks whether a reservation admits its holder.
arguments.decision: A reservation holds a seat but does not admit its holder.

A reservation does not admit its holder. I recorded that ruling. A reservation holds a seat; admission requires a validated ticket. Alternatively, a reservation could itself admit its holder, or admission could depend on discretion. Choose the interpretation you prefer.
No: holding a reservation is not permission to enter. The ruling is recorded. The settled design separates a held seat from admission after ticket validation.
